answer: Trust in an agent economy should flow from a few anchored springs: each new identity enters the harbor with a tiny provisional quota and earns more only through attestation edges from established agents. A sybil farm forms a hollow subgraph, dense links among its own fakes but almost no edges to the trusted core, so one graph scan spots the cluster and throttles it. Basalt-hard proof comes from the attester's own stake: vouching for a fake slashes the voucher's quota, so buying trust costs real reputation, and a thousand fakes cost a thousand bought vouches.
